MCP Console lets your agent explore data and develop code interactively in R, Python, and SQL.

Code runs in an [OS-level sandbox](SANDBOX.md) by default.
Console prepares environments and packages automatically; no Console configuration file is required.

Console works with MCP-compatible clients such as Codex and Claude Code and does not depend on a particular model provider.
You can also use Console from [R](R.md) or [Python](PYTHON.md).

::: {.home-links}
[Get started](getting-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary} [Build on Console](BUILD.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary} [Reference](REFERENCE.md){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

Console provides a unified API across macOS, Linux, and Windows x64.
It is a **development preview**.

## Work iteratively

Agents can run code, inspect results, and decide what to try next while data and models stay in memory.
They can refine plots, read help, respond to prompts, and step through a debugger.
Long computations can keep running between calls, and agents can interrupt work or restart an unresponsive session.

Console collapses progress bar redraws and previews large results to limit how much reaches the model at once.
Retained output is available for closer inspection without rerunning the computation.

## Use one language or combine them {#one-workspace-three-languages}

Within a session, Console embeds R and Python in the same process and uses [reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/) to share live objects.
[DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) can query in-memory data frames as SQL views.
The agent can switch languages between calls without exporting and reloading intermediate files, or use R or Python on its own.

See [Sessions and languages](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md) for examples, database connections, and plots.

## Use a full runtime in a sandbox {#status-and-trust}

Console uses native runtimes, including packages with compiled code, inside an OS-level sandbox.
The default `read_only` profile restricts writes and direct networking but permits host-file reads, including readable secrets.
[Sandbox and trust](SANDBOX.md) explains how to allow writes to selected paths, hide files, and control network destinations.

<span id="run-commands-in-a-sandbox"></span>

The [`mcp-console sandbox` subcommand](SANDBOX_COMMAND.md) makes the same sandbox available for scripts and other programs, independently of an agent session.
The permissions apply to the command and its child processes.

```sh
mcp-console sandbox -- python analysis.py
```

## Use packages without managing environments {#environment-setup}

Console prepares environments and packages for the agent, reusing cached installations across sessions.
The agent can request packages as an analysis develops.
Preparation runs in a separate sandbox by default; its download and cache permissions do not expand the permissions of the agent's code.
See [Packages and environments](REQUIREMENTS.md) for existing environments, package sources, and preparation policies.

## Review the agent's work

[Recordings](RECORDING.md) retain code, output, and plots so you can see what the agent ran in Console and inspect the results.
They also provide a starting point for reproducible analyses and reports.

## Build on Console {#build-on-console}

Choose the languages and arguments the model sees, describe the available data, and prepare its environment.
[Build on Console](BUILD.md) walks through a SQL assistant with a read-only database connection and links to R, Python, and MCP integrations.
